## Welcome to the Flora of the Saanich Peninsula

The Saanich Peninsula is part of the homeland of the W̱SÁNEĆ people, whose knowledge of its plants and landscapes
extends back countless generations. Among the region's published botanical references, Szczawinski and Harrison’s
(1972) *Flora of the Saanich Peninsula* remains a classic. Harvey Janszen devoted much of his life to revising this
work but passed away before completing it. Local naturalists have since carried his efforts forward, and this website
shares that continuing legacy.

To date, `r format(nrow(plant.summary), big.mark = ",")` vascular plant species have been recorded on the Saanich
Peninsula, but many have not been seen in recent years. Some may be lost *to us*—overlooked, forgotten, or waiting to
be rediscovered. Others may be lost *because of us*, through habitat change and invasive species.

We’re bringing together local naturalists and community members to search for these “lost” plants, update the
historical flora, and better understand how biodiversity is changing across the Saanich Peninsula.

Explore the map and tabs above to discover which species may still be out there, and join the search through the
**[“Lost” Plants of the Saanich Peninsula](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/lost-plants-of-the-saanich-peninsula)**
project on iNaturalist.
